key_insight: A repeatable, evidence-based evaluation framework shows how prompt design systematically influences LLM-generated follow-up questions—affecting pedagogical alignment and personalization in educational dialogues.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic methods for designing and evaluating prompts that produce pedagogically aligned, personalized outputs from LLMs in educational settings.
method: Design six prompt templates that vary pedagogical guidance and personalization constraints.
Generate follow-up questions from an LLM within a structured dialogue activity and annotate outputs for alignment, relevance, and personalization.
Compare template performance using quantitative and qualitative criteria to identify which prompt features yield more pedagogically useful responses.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and edtech designers a practical, generalizable workflow to iterate on prompt design and reliably measure educational quality—enabling safer, more effective LLM integration in learning tools.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the evaluation pipeline: prompt design → LLM generation → annotation → analysis
Bar or radar chart comparing templates across metrics (alignment, relevance, personalization, coherence)
Side-by-side example panel: prompt template vs. generated follow-up question vs. human annotation
Icons representing pedagogy, personalization, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility
paper_title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
paper_authors: Langdon Holmes, Adam Coscia, Scott Crossley, Joon Suh Choi, Wesley Morris
